I'm 76 years old this year. Never went to school, can't read those papers the extension office hands out. Only been farming on my own for one year — before that, my younger brother handled the land, but he moved to the city and left me these 5.5 mu. It's just me and my wife now, two old people eating off this dirt. My back isn't what it used to be, and my knees hurt when it rains, so I have to hire young folks for anything heavy.

I don't really know what I'm doing, to be honest. Last year was my first time making the decisions myself, and I mostly copied Old Wang from the next courtyard. He knows everything — what day to plant, which bags to buy from the shop, when the water needs to come. If Old Wang does something, I do it too. That's my whole strategy.

I keep 3 mu in wheat-maize, same as most folks around here. That's our food security — even if prices are bad, we have grain in the bin. The other 2.5 mu I plant cotton, because Old Wang said the money is better than maize some years, and last year the cotton buyer paid cash on the spot. Though I have to say, picking cotton at my age is torture. I bend down and my head spins. This might be the last year I do cotton, but I'll try again.

**Wheat:** I plant around October 10th, same day as Old Wang. I buy the ordinary seed from the village supply shop — not the fancy kind, just the regular one everyone uses. About 12 kg per mu, costs me maybe 45 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — the shop sells them in 50 kg bags. Then when the wheat starts growing tall in March, I topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. Old Wang says do it at jointing, when the stems get that little bump. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once in spring at jointing, and once when the grains are filling. The well water isn't free — every time I pump, the meter runs and I wince — but you can't skip it or the yield dies. I spray herbicide once after planting, and maybe fungicide if I see disease.

**Maize:** This goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 10th. The window is cruel — sometimes only five or six days between cutting wheat and putting maize in the ground! Last year I was too slow and the seedlings came up uneven. This year I'll hire the tractor driver to turn the soil quick, and hire two young men to help plant. I buy hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the planting furrow. If the leaves turn yellow later, I might add a bit of urea, but usually once is enough. Irrigate twice — once after planting, once at tasseling if there's no rain.

**Cotton:** Planted mid-April. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and some farmyard manure I scraped from the courtyard. Cotton needs spraying for insects — last year the bollworms came and I nearly lost everything. I'll spray three times this year, insecticide and herbicide. Irrigate twice. But the picking — four times from September to October! I can't bend down like that. I'll hire the village women to pick, pay them by the jin. That's my biggest expense, but without it, the cotton rots in the field.

For labor, my wife and me can handle spreading fertilizer, watching the fields, and cooking for hired hands — maybe 15 family days total. But for planting, harvest, tractor work, and especially cotton picking, I need hired help. Probably 36 hired days at 100 yuan each. That's 3,600 yuan just for labor.

Total costs? Seed maybe 400 yuan, fertilizer about 1,500 yuan, pesticide 500 yuan, water pumping 700 yuan, hired labor 3,600 yuan... I reckon about 6,600 yuan total. That's almost all the cash I have. If drought hits or prices drop, we're eating into next year's seed money. But what choice do I have? I do what Old Wang does, pray the weather holds, and hope I get through another year.

Yield? Last year my wheat was only 380 kg per mu — I was still learning. This year I hope for 400 kg. Maize maybe 450 kg. Cotton... last year I got about 220 kg per mu of seed cotton. I'll be happy with the same. I don't expect miracles. I just want enough to eat, enough to buy medicine, and maybe a little left over.
